scope_note: Retires eager raw asset registration through shared prepared resources and commit-controlled publication. Raw per-command execution and atomic queue adoption preserve their distinct documented policies. External transport/queues, presentation transform overrides, whole-scene replacement and asynchronous resource readiness/performance remain separate work. F2 remains active.
integration_findings: Removed native register_animation_assets from submission; simulation submission has no asset-registry publication.
Core uses a host preparation/publication contract without depending on the asset store. Native project, preview and stage worlds install the same source through set_assets.
Reuses PreparedGameplayResources for clips/blends/controllers/skins/sounds/collider meshes/materials. Controller staging is shared with owned gameplay sessions.
Raw command preflight precedes journal publication; prepared resources publish after accepted data and before committed playback delivery.
Atomic queue adoption preflights a deduplicated union, retaining queue, data and registries on failure.

Six new prepared-resource tests and one real C-ABI test cover inert submission, rejection, capacity, adoption rollback and deduplication, sound delivery/no replay, mesh/skin rejection, and successful raw publication.
Preparation occurs synchronously at execution/adoption against the currently installed asset source. This is not an asynchronous loading or performance qualification claim.
